    # Read all source files and concatenate
    dfs = []
    for file_path in source_files:
        df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
        # Ensure columns are exactly as target schema
        df = df[target_columns]

        # Convert data types to target schema
        # For episodes and members, use nullable integer type to handle any missing values safely
        df['anime_id'] = pd.to_numeric(df['anime_id'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')
        df['name'] = df['name'].astype('string')
        df['genre'] = df['genre'].astype('string')
        df['type'] = df['type'].astype('string')
        df['episodes'] = pd.to_numeric(df['episodes'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')
        df['rating'] = pd.to_numeric(df['rating'], errors='coerce').astype('float64')
        df['members'] = pd.to_numeric(df['members'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

        dfs.append(df)

    # Concatenate all dataframes
    combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # Remove duplicates if any (based on all columns)
    combined_df = combined_df.drop_duplicates()

    # Optional: Sort by anime_id for neatness
    combined_df = combined_df.sort_values(by='anime_id').reset_index(drop=True)

    # Write to target CSV
    output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_75/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    combined_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
